title: 2 Secrets Hidden Inside the Pagani Utopia

scenes.text: Before one single Pagani Utopia reached a customer, the company built eight complete prototypes, twelve scale models, and spent more than six years on the project. Three of those prototypes existed only to test the engine, for about two years. And the result is a car that, by its maker's own words, has no hybrid system and no dual-clutch gearbox. This is the Pagani Utopia, and there are two things about it that you probably did not know.
scenes.caption: 2 SECRETS HIDDEN INSIDE THE PAGANI UTOPIA

scenes.text: The first is about a gearbox that almost nobody asked a carmaker for in the twenty twenties, and why Pagani built it anyway. The second is about what is hiding inside the carbon structure, where one car contains more than forty different recipes of material. Both are verified in published sources, and we will show you where.
scenes.caption: THE GEARBOX · THE CARBON RECIPES

scenes.text: Every fact in this video comes from published sources, listed in the description. Where sources disagree, we will tell you. Where we do the maths ourselves, we will say so. Let us begin with the car.
scenes.caption: EVERY FACT IS SOURCED

scenes.text: Wikipedia says the Pagani Utopia was unveiled on the twelfth of September, twenty twenty-two, at the Teatro Lirico in Milan. It is Pagani's third model, after the Zonda and the Huayra, and it is built in San Cesario sul Panaro, in Italy. Its internal code is C ten, following the C eight of the Zonda and the C nine of the Huayra.
scenes.caption: UNVEILED IN MILAN, 12 SEPTEMBER 2022

scenes.text: The engine is a five point nine eight litre Mercedes-AMG twin-turbocharged V twelve. Wikipedia lists eight hundred sixty-four metric horsepower at six thousand r p m, and eleven hundred newton-metres of torque, available between two thousand eight hundred and five thousand nine hundred r p m. The engine alone weighs two hundred sixty-two kilograms, dry.
scenes.caption: 864 PS · 1,100 NM · 262 KG ENGINE

scenes.text: It is a rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive car. The dry weight is one thousand two hundred eighty kilograms. By our own arithmetic, the engine is therefore about twenty percent of the whole car. Wikipedia lists the length at four thousand five hundred ninety-seven millimetres and the height at one thousand one hundred sixty-nine, a low, wide shape.
scenes.caption: 1,280 KG DRY · RWD · MID-ENGINE

scenes.text: Top Gear reports that only ninety-nine coupés will be built, at around two point two million pounds each, and that they were all already allocated. Wikipedia says the first car was delivered in October twenty twenty-three, with pricing starting at two point one nine million dollars.
scenes.caption: 99 COUPÉS · ALL SOLD BEFORE DELIVERY

scenes.text: Supercar Blondie quoted the starting price as two million, one hundred seventy thousand euros, just under two point two million dollars. So the sources differ a little, by currency and date. In every one of them, the Utopia is a car that costs about as much as a luxury house, and that was spoken for before anyone drove it.
scenes.caption: €2,170,000 AT LAUNCH

scenes.text: Compare it with the car it replaced. The Huayra, according to Wikipedia, had a six litre twin-turbo Mercedes-AMG V twelve with seven hundred forty metric horsepower and one thousand newton-metres. By our own arithmetic, the Utopia's eight hundred sixty-four is almost seventeen percent more power, and its eleven hundred newton-metres is ten percent more torque.
scenes.caption: VS HUAYRA: +17% POWER, +10% TORQUE

scenes.text: Top Gear says the new engine revs higher and is more flexible than the one it supersedes. The torque figure supports that. Wikipedia says the eleven hundred newton-metres is available between two thousand eight hundred and five thousand nine hundred r p m. By our arithmetic, that is a band more than three thousand r p m wide.
scenes.caption: PEAK TORQUE FROM 2,800 TO 5,900 RPM

scenes.text: The timeline is also unusual. Wikipedia gives the unveiling as September twenty twenty-two and the first delivery as October twenty twenty-three. By our own arithmetic, that is thirteen months. And Pagani unveiled the roadster only twenty-two months after the coupé, in July twenty twenty-four, with a hundred thirty examples planned.
scenes.caption: 13 MONTHS FROM UNVEILING TO FIRST DELIVERY

scenes.text: Now the first thing you probably did not know. Wikipedia says the Utopia was developed over more than six years. In that time, Pagani built eight complete prototypes. Three of them were used for about two years of engine testing alone. Imagine building three entire cars just so one engine could be tested.
scenes.caption: 6+ YEARS · 8 PROTOTYPES
scenes.chapter: Secret one begins: six years of development

scenes.text: Wikipedia says the team also made twelve scale models: ten at one-fifth scale and two at full size. Supercar Blondie adds that the design process involved thousands of sketches. So before the Utopia existed as a car, it existed as a pile of drawings and a small fleet of models in clay or other materials.
scenes.caption: 12 SCALE MODELS · THOUSANDS OF SKETCHES

scenes.text: By our own arithmetic, there is a pattern. Eight prototypes for ninety-nine coupés is roughly one prototype for every twelve customer cars. A mass-market car maker would need to build hundreds of thousands of cars to justify that ratio. Pagani needs ninety-nine.
scenes.caption: 1 PROTOTYPE FOR EVERY ~12 COUPÉS

scenes.text: Why so many? Top Gear says Pagani's brief was to re-engage with simplicity, lightness and the pleasure of driving. The company says the engine meets California's emissions rules too. So the engineers had to make a twin-turbo V twelve that is clean enough for California, light enough for Pagani, and exciting enough for a three million dollar buyer.
scenes.caption: CLEAN ENOUGH FOR CALIFORNIA

scenes.text: Top Gear quotes Horacio Pagani saying there are no heavy batteries and no hybrid power, just a wonderful V twelve. In an age when almost every hypercar adds electric motors, that was a choice. And the choice was not an accident. It was a six-year decision, tested on three prototypes.
scenes.caption: "NO HYBRID POWER, JUST A WONDERFUL V12"

scenes.text: The Wikipedia page also says the suspension is forged aluminium double-wishbone, based on experience from the track-only Huayra R. So even the road car borrows from a car that never touched a public road. Racing knowledge flows into the Utopia through the chassis.
scenes.caption: SUSPENSION FROM THE TRACK-ONLY HUAYRA R

scenes.text: Pagani's own roadster press release goes further. It says the eight suspension triangles are forged in aircraft-grade aluminium alloy. Eight triangles, four wheels, two on each corner. That is a lot of expensive metal for parts most owners will never see, and it is typical of how this company thinks.
scenes.caption: 8 SUSPENSION ARMS, AIRCRAFT-GRADE

scenes.text: Weight was always Pagani's obsession. The Attic Capital summary of an interview quotes Horacio Pagani saying he has a weight mania. It tells how, when he first put the Mercedes V twelve for the Zonda on the scale, it weighed seventy kilograms less than the Lamborghini Diablo engine he had designed around. Twenty years later, the habit is intact.
scenes.caption: "I HAVE A WEIGHT MANIA"

scenes.text: Now to the gearbox. Wikipedia says the Utopia has a seven-speed Xtrac gearbox, mounted transversely, offered as a pure manual or an automated manual. It pairs with an electro-mechanical differential through a triple-plate clutch. In plain words, you can have three pedals in a car with more than eight hundred horsepower.
scenes.caption: A TRUE MANUAL IN A 864 PS CAR
scenes.chapter: Secret one: the gearbox nobody expected

scenes.text: Supercar Blondie says it is a special seven-speed unit made by Xtrac just for this car, in both versions. And it quotes why Pagani built the manual: offering one was especially important, because it is what customers demanded. So the manual is not nostalgia from the company. It is an answer to the people paying for the car.
scenes.caption: BUILT BY XTRAC, JUST FOR THIS CAR

scenes.text: Top Gear adds another detail, with a bit of humour. The article says there will be no virtual manual, and it quotes the company: no dual-clutch system, just a pure seven-speed manual or automated transmission. The automated version, Top Gear says, is lighter, more compact and uses helical gears. It is not a dual-clutch.
scenes.caption: NO DUAL-CLUTCH

scenes.text: That matters because almost every modern hypercar uses a dual-clutch gearbox, which changes gear in a fraction of a second. Pagani chose neither that nor a hybrid motor. By our reading of the sources, it chose the opposite approach: fewer parts, more feel, and an engine that stays in charge.
scenes.caption: FEWER PARTS, MORE FEEL

scenes.text: The roadster press release describes the clutch as light and adjustable, a triple-disc clutch. That is an engineering answer to a human problem. A clutch that is too heavy would make an expensive car tiring in traffic, and one that is too light would feel numb. Pagani says it made the pedal light and adjustable.
scenes.caption: A LIGHT, ADJUSTABLE TRIPLE-DISC CLUTCH

scenes.text: Now compare it with the Zonda. Wikipedia lists the Zonda Cinque of two thousand nine with a six-speed automated manual that shifts in under one hundred milliseconds. The Utopia goes back to the manual idea, with seven speeds. Sixteen years apart, Pagani used the same gearbox philosophy in an opposite direction.
scenes.caption: ZONDA CINQUE: 6-SPEED AUTOMATED MANUAL

scenes.text: The Zonda C twelve itself, according to Wikipedia, came out in nineteen ninety-nine with a six litre Mercedes V twelve. So the Utopia's engine, at nearly six litres, shows the same family idea twenty-three years later, now twin-turbocharged and built specially for Pagani, according to Top Gear.
scenes.caption: FROM A 1999 V12 TO A 2022 TWIN-TURBO V12

scenes.text: There is a second reason that the manual matters. Wikipedia says the Utopia is rear-wheel drive with an electro-mechanical differential. With no front motor to help, all eight hundred sixty-four horsepower reaches the road through the rear wheels. A car like that is a very direct machine, and a manual gearbox makes it even more so.
scenes.caption: ALL THE POWER THROUGH THE REAR WHEELS

scenes.text: We should be honest about what the sources do not say. Top Gear's launch article does not give an acceleration time or a top speed, and the Wikipedia page for the Utopia lists none. So we do not quote any. Pagani has not published a number that we could find, and we will not repeat a figure from a forum or a video.
scenes.caption: NO OFFICIAL 0–100 OR TOP SPEED FOUND

scenes.text: Now the second thing. Pagani's roadster press release says there are over forty formulas of composite materials within the same hypercar. Read that again. Not forty parts. Forty different recipes. Each one mixes fibres, resins and layers in a particular way, to give a particular combination of strength, weight and stiffness.
scenes.caption: 40+ COMPOSITE FORMULAS IN ONE CAR
scenes.chapter: Secret two: more than forty recipes of carbon

scenes.text: The same release names two of them: Carbo-Titanium HP sixty-two G two, and Carbo-Triax HP sixty-two. Carbo-titanium is Pagani's own name for a carbon fibre material woven with titanium. Top Gear says the car's structure is a carbo-titanium monocoque, with tubular alloy steel subframes at the front and rear.
scenes.caption: CARBO-TITANIUM HP62-G2 · CARBO-TRIAX HP62

scenes.text: Why do forty formulas matter? Because every part of a car has a different job. The part that holds the engine needs stiffness. A panel on the nose needs lightness. A part near the exhaust needs heat resistance. Using a different recipe for each is expensive and slow, which is exactly why mass-made cars do not do it.
scenes.caption: DIFFERENT PARTS, DIFFERENT RECIPES

scenes.text: The press release says the monocoque was entirely redesigned to optimise rigidity and resistance. And the carbon-titanium monocoque gives, in the company's words, an exceptional ratio, presumably of strength to weight. We are quoting the company here, and there is no independent test in our sources.
scenes.caption: A MONOCOQUE ENTIRELY REDESIGNED

scenes.text: There is a history behind this obsession. Wikipedia says Horacio Pagani formerly created and managed Lamborghini's composites department, and in nineteen eighty-eight founded Pagani Composite Research. So the man who designed the Utopia spent decades learning to make carbon fibre parts, long before he built a car of his own.
scenes.caption: A CAREER BUILT ON CARBON FIBRE

scenes.text: That also explains the weight. Wikipedia says the Utopia weighs one thousand two hundred eighty kilograms dry. The Zonda R, a track version, weighs one thousand seventy, and the first Zonda C twelve weighed one thousand two hundred fifty. By our own arithmetic, the Utopia is only thirty kilograms heavier than a nineteen ninety-nine Zonda.
scenes.caption: ONLY 30 KG HEAVIER THAN A 1999 ZONDA

scenes.text: Think about what that means. In twenty-three years, the engine got more powerful, the car got larger, safety rules got stricter, and customers wanted air conditioning, screens and comfort. Yet the dry weight went up by only thirty kilograms. We do not claim this is easy. We say the sources show that it is true.
scenes.caption: 23 YEARS, +30 KG

scenes.text: Interior materials follow the same attitude. The roadster press release lists leather named Grecale and Huayra Signature, and describes an optional Sport Pack with seats in leather lightened by twenty percent. A twenty percent lighter leather is the kind of detail only a company obsessed with weight would bother to develop.
scenes.caption: LEATHER LIGHTENED BY 20%

scenes.text: The roadster has another surprise, according to the same release. With the hard top in place there is a single large roof window. And the hard top can be displayed on a stand when it is not on the car, which tells you what Pagani thinks of its own carbon work. It is meant to be looked at.
scenes.caption: THE HARD-TOP CAN BE A DISPLAY PIECE

scenes.text: Supercar Blondie describes more details. The rear taillights are suspended and take their influence from jet turbines. The elliptical centre section of the rear bumper includes active aero flaps. And Pagani's hallmarks remain: four central exhaust tips and butterfly doors.
scenes.caption: JET-TURBINE TAILLIGHTS

scenes.text: The same article quotes a surprising description of the wing mirrors: the eye of a beautiful woman. And it says the headlight fairings reference the nineteen fifties and sixties. So the Utopia mixes modern engineering with shapes that look back, a design choice rather than a technical one.
scenes.caption: MIRRORS "LIKE THE EYE OF A BEAUTIFUL WOMAN"

scenes.text: Inside, Supercar Blondie says all of the instrumentation is analogue, aside from one small screen for the driver. In a time of giant displays, that is another unusual decision. Top Gear says the name Utopia comes from a work by Sir Thomas More, and describes a car with simple, flowing, curvaceous lines.
scenes.caption: ANALOGUE GAUGES, ONE SMALL SCREEN

scenes.text: Top Gear also notes that the Utopia lacks the large wings, splitters and vents typical of Pagani. The company hints at special editions with more aerodynamics later. So the first Utopia is, by Pagani's standards, restrained. A hypercar that tries not to shout is a surprise in itself.
scenes.caption: A PAGANI THAT DOESN'T SHOUT

scenes.text: Top Gear cites Pagani saying that each car begins with an aesthetic shock. That sounds like marketing, but the company has a record. Its first car, the Zonda, was understood instantly at the Geneva show in nineteen ninety-nine, according to the book quoted by Attic Capital, which credits it with popularising the word hypercar.
scenes.caption: "AN AESTHETIC SHOCK"

scenes.text: The press release even makes a game of colour. The presentation car had new roadster wheels in brushed silver on the driver's side, and Aeroblade wheels in Pearl Beige with a diamond-cut finish on the passenger side. Two different wheel designs on one car, as a way of showing what a customer could ask for.
scenes.caption: TWO DIFFERENT WHEELS ON ONE CAR

scenes.text: Top Gear lists the wheels as twenty-one inch at the front and twenty-two at the rear, forged aluminium. The brakes are carbon ceramic ventilated discs, with six-piston calipers at the front and four-piston at the rear. Suspension has electronically managed active dampers. Nothing there is simple, even though the car is.
scenes.caption: 21-INCH FRONT · 22-INCH REAR

scenes.text: The roadster press release says the standard tyres are Pirelli P Zero Corsa and P Zero Winter, with P Zero Trofeo R S optional. A Pagani on winter tyres is, in our reading, a sign of a customer who actually drives the car. Pagani seems to expect owners to use it.
scenes.caption: STANDARD: PIRELLI P ZERO CORSA & WINTER

scenes.text: Wikipedia says the Utopia roadster was introduced on the thirtieth of July, twenty twenty-four, with production limited to one hundred thirty units. It has a removable carbon fibre hard top and a soft top, and it keeps the coupé's powertrain. The base price is three point four million dollars, or three point one million euros.
scenes.caption: ROADSTER: 130 CARS · FROM €3.1M

scenes.text: Pagani's press release says the roadster weighs the same as the coupé, one thousand two hundred eighty kilograms, and that the two were developed jointly. Earlier Pagani roadsters, such as the Zonda and Huayra roadsters, came after the coupés. This time, the open car was designed together with the closed one.
scenes.caption: COUPÉ AND ROADSTER DEVELOPED TOGETHER

scenes.text: The release also says the soft top is stored in a suitcase, in place of the vanity case, and describes the presentation colour as exposed carbon in Habanero Red, which shifts from a brownish red in the shade to a bright red in the sun. Even the luggage is part of the design.
scenes.caption: A SUITCASE FOR THE SOFT TOP

scenes.text: By our own arithmetic, ninety-nine coupés and one hundred thirty roadsters make two hundred twenty-nine production cars. At the base prices quoted, about two point one seven million euros for the coupé and three point one for the roadster, the order book is roughly six hundred million euros. That is an estimate, without options.
scenes.caption: ~229 CARS · ~€600M AT BASE PRICES

scenes.text: Think about the customer's side. Wikipedia lists the customers it knows from Pagani's history, among them Benny Caiola, the first Pagani customer, after whom the Huayra B C was named, and Lewis Hamilton, who is listed with a Zonda seven hundred sixty L H. These are people who know exactly what they are buying, which is why a manual matters.
scenes.caption: THE FIRST CUSTOMER: BENNY CAIOLA

scenes.text: There is also a link back to the Zonda's own story. Wikipedia says the Zonda was originally planned as the Fangio F one, after the five-time world champion Juan Manuel Fangio, and was renamed after his death in nineteen ninety-five. The Utopia, nearly three decades later, still follows the idea of a driver's car built by hand.
scenes.caption: FROM THE FANGIO F1 TO THE UTOPIA

scenes.text: Scale is one more surprise. Wikipedia says that as of twenty nineteen, a hundred forty Zondas had been built over twenty years, including development cars. The Utopia plans ninety-nine coupés and a hundred thirty roadsters. By our own arithmetic, that is two hundred twenty-nine cars, about sixty-four percent more than the whole Zonda run.
scenes.caption: UTOPIA PLAN: 229 CARS · ZONDA TOTAL: 140

scenes.text: That tells you how much the company has grown since nineteen ninety-nine, when the first Zonda was shown in Geneva. Yet two hundred twenty-nine cars is still a very small number. For Pagani, it is a full generation of work, by our reading.
scenes.caption: STILL TINY BY CARMAKER STANDARDS

scenes.text: So here are the two secrets again. First, a gearbox: a true manual built by Xtrac for this car, because Pagani's customers asked for it. Second, a recipe book: more than forty composite formulas in a single car, around a carbo-titanium monocoque. Both come from published sources, and both show how unusual this company is.
scenes.caption: A TRUE MANUAL · 40+ COMPOSITE RECIPES

scenes.text: Add the numbers. Six years of development, eight prototypes, twelve scale models, an engine that weighs two hundred sixty-two kilograms, and a car that weighs one thousand two hundred eighty. All of it for ninety-nine coupés that were sold before the first one left the factory. That is the Pagani way.
scenes.caption: 6 YEARS · 8 PROTOTYPES · 99 CARS

scenes.text: Which of the two secrets surprised you more, the manual gearbox or the forty recipes of carbon? Tell us in the comments. In the other videos of this series, we compare the Utopia with the Zonda, work out what it really costs to own a Pagani, and tell the story of Horacio Pagani.
scenes.caption: WHICH SECRET SURPRISED YOU MORE?

scenes.text: And if you want to spend your money on something you can actually drive every day, our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality for more stories about the cars and trucks people really talk about.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
